title: Max for Live's buffer~ does not read Ableton's encrypted factory samples from inside Live's process, and the AIFC container is not the reason
set: empty set, four tracks, no clips; the device on audio track index 2
question: Offline, an 'able' compression type marks a same size transform of the SSND payload and no key is published, so no external decoder can read it. Max runs inside Live's process and might reach Live's own decoder. Does buffer~ read these files?

answers.state_before_this_record: open question, and asserted closed in the commit message of 073348b on the strength of the offline finding alone
answers.answered_in: A question raised in working notes kept outside the repository, under "3. Die Max-for-Live-"Hoeren"-Idee". This record is the published answer.

method: The device holds one buffer~. A request names a file; the device sends it 'replace', which resizes the buffer to the file rather than truncating it to the buffer's length.

buffer~ bangs its right outlet when a read completes and does not bang it when one fails, so an unanswered request is the read failing. The device answers with what info~ reports: sample rate, total length in milliseconds and channel count.

A second request has the device write the buffer out with 'writewave'. That dump is read in Python and measured, because a length is not a decode: a reader that parses the header and fails on the payload still reports the right length. Peak, RMS, crest factor and zero crossing rate separate audio from silence and from full scale noise.
Every encrypted file is probed against plain uncompressed controls in the same run, so the shape of a correct dump is measured on this machine on this day rather than assumed.
The classifier was checked first against three files whose contents were known: a real one shot, a synthesised silence and synthesised white noise. It answered audio, silent and noise.

readings.encrypted_outcome: read_failed, meaning buffer~ never banged completion inside 20 seconds
readings.control_containers: ten AIFF with compression NONE, and one AIFC
readings.live_was_never_blocked: The controls ran after the encrypted files in every run and answered normally, so the silence is the read failing rather than Live hanging on a dialog.

container_control.why: If buffer~ simply could not read AIFC, that would look exactly like a failure to decrypt, and the conclusion would be different: a container rewrite would reach the audio.
container_control.file: Factory Packs/Convolution Reverb/IRs/09 Springs/Moist Spring Mono.aif
container_control.conclusion: buffer~ reads AIFC. What it does not read is the encryption.

library_scale.note: Of the .aif files under these two roots, 97.4 percent are encrypted. This is one machine's installed packs and is not a statement about Ableton's catalogue.

result: The Max route to Ableton's encrypted factory samples is closed. Running inside Live's process does not give buffer~ the decoder.
The offline conclusion was right and the reasoning behind it was not sufficient: not being able to decrypt from Python says nothing about Max. This record is the test that was owed.

sample_match can read the User Library and the plain part of the factory content and must report the encrypted part as unreadable rather than skipping it silently. No afconvert detour helps either, since the obstacle is the encryption and not the container.
scope_and_weakness: Eleven encrypted files out of 19,725, drawn from a shuffled list with a fixed seed. Nothing here rules out a pack whose files behave differently.
One machine, one Live version, one installation, one set of pack licences. A file this installation is not licensed for is not distinguishable here from one it cannot decrypt at all.
Only buffer~ was tried. Other objects that read files were not, and neither was the possibility that Live decodes into memory somewhere a Max object could reach by another route.
The failure is an absence of a reply inside 20 seconds. That is the documented signature of a failed read, but it is an absence, and an absence has more than one cause.
Nothing here was done with a device of Ableton's own, such as Simpler, which plays these files: the finding is about what a Max object can read, not about what Live can play.
recorded_also_in_note: This record is the only published account of the measurement. What it also went into at the time were working notes kept outside the repository.
